summary: 7 functional and 3 non-functional requirements; 9 ambiguities recorded (9 assumptions, 0 unresolved).
decisions: What HTTP method and route should expose the expiry-change operation?: Add an additive `PATCH /links/{linkId}` operation, retaining any existing API base path or version prefix used by the service. (assumption)

How should a request distinguish setting an expiry, removing it, and omitting an expiry value?: Use the `expiresAt` field and the same timestamp format and parsing rules as link creation. A future timestamp sets the expiry; `null` removes it; an omitted `expiresAt` field is rejected with HTTP 400 and leaves the link unchanged. (assumption)
What success response should an expiry-change request return?: Return HTTP 200 with the updated link metadata, including the new expiry or the absence of an expiry. (assumption)

How should the management token be sent, and what response should be used for a missing or invalid token?: Use the service's existing management-token authentication mechanism and its existing authentication-failure response; do not mutate the link when authentication fails. (assumption)

What format and location should be used for the machine-readable API definition and operator and API-client documentation?: Use an OpenAPI 3.x definition and place it and the operator and API-client documentation in the service's established documentation locations and formats. (assumption)

What form should the changelog entry and release-readiness review take?: Use the repository's established changelog and release-review formats; record completion of the review before shipment, including the change's verification, compatibility, and documentation readiness. (assumption)
